page.title: Portable Power Station for a TV: Measured Hours at TV-Size Loads
page.h1: Portable power station for a TV: the hours you get at TV-size loads
page.desc: A TV is a small AC load, so a power station's inverter idle draw cuts into its capacity. This page uses measured low-load output for the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2, EcoFlow RIVER 2 Max, BLUETTI AC70, Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 and EcoFlow DELTA 3 Classic.
page.answer: Short answer. A TV is a small AC load, so inverter idle draw eats capacity. The BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 (1,024 Wh) gives about 80% of its capacity as AC output under 100 W, which is about 16 hours of a 50 W TV. The EcoFlow RIVER 2 Max gives about 7.

page.after:
What the differences mean

  • Hours of a 50 W TV. Elite 100 V2: 1,024 Wh × 80% ≈ 819 Wh, and 819 ÷ 50 ≈ 16.4 h. AC70: 623 ÷ 50 ≈ 12.5 h. RIVER 2 Max: 499 Wh × 71.5% ≈ 357 Wh, and 357 ÷ 50 ≈ 7.1 h.
  • Cost per Wh a TV can actually use. Elite 100 V2: $499 ÷ 819 Wh ≈ $0.61. RIVER 2 Max: $309 ÷ 357 Wh ≈ $0.87. AC70: $359 ÷ 623 Wh ≈ $0.58, but it is sold out.
  • Share of the draw that goes to the inverter with a 50 W TV. AC70: 8 ÷ 58 ≈ 14%. Elite 100 V2: 16 ÷ 66 ≈ 24%. DELTA 3 Classic: 17 ÷ 67 ≈ 25%. C1000 Gen 2: 17 ÷ 67 ≈ 25%.
  • The makers' own TV figures. BLUETTI lists the Elite 100 V2 at 8.9 h for an 85 W TV: 85 × 8.9 ≈ 757 Wh, or 74% of 1,024 Wh. It lists the AC70 at 8.2 h for a 65 W TV: 65 × 8.2 ≈ 533 Wh, or 69% of 768 Wh. Both are well below a flat 85% assumption.

The DELTA 3 Classic is a close call. The Solar Lab measured it at about 83% inverter efficiency with a 17 W idle, against about 80% and 16 W for the Elite 100 V2, and it costs $40 less. No reviewer has published its output at a TV-size load. The Elite 100 V2 has been measured at under-100 W loads, and BLUETTI rates it for 4,000+ cycles to 80% capacity, so it is the pick when you want the TV hours confirmed: {buy:bluetti-elite-100-v2}. If price decides it, the DELTA 3 Classic is the better buy.

Why a TV gets less than the label says

An inverter draws a fixed number of watts just to stay on, whatever is plugged in. With a 500 W load that overhead hardly matters. With a 50 W TV it is a quarter of the draw. Michael Barton at techtest.org measured the AC70 at 81% of rated capacity at 50 W, 91% at 250 W and 92% at 500 W. He measured the RIVER 2 Max at 71.5% at 50 W, 72.9% at 150 W and 73.6% at 500 W. Timo Altmeyer at Techreviewer.de got 946 Wh (93%) from the Elite 100 V2 at 500 W, but only about 80% at loads in the double digits. Notebookcheck's 850 Wh for the C1000 Gen 2 was measured at about 250 W, so a small TV will get less than 850 ÷ 50 hours. The techtest, Techreviewer and Notebookcheck tests used 230 V units, and US 120 V units can measure differently.

Two settings can switch the TV off. BLUETTI's AC70 manual says ECO Mode is on by default and turns AC output off when the load stays under 40 W. You can turn ECO Mode off. Gidon at The Technology Man found that the C1000 Gen 2, by default, turns its inverter off after 15 minutes under 20 W. A dimmed small TV or a set in standby can fall below either limit, so switch these modes off before an outage. {buy:anker-solix-c1000-gen-2}

Not recommended right now

BLUETTI AC70. It has the lowest measured idle draw here (about 8 W), but every variant was out of stock at BLUETTI US on 2026-11-13, and the page still gives an 'Early September' restock date. For a 768 Wh budget station you can buy today, look elsewhere until it comes back.
